title: How Florida Weather Affects a House Painting Job
description: Humidity, dew point, surface heat, and afternoon storms decide when exterior paint can go on in Florida. How weather shapes a painting schedule.
h1: How Florida Weather Affects a House Painting Project
heroIntro: Exterior paint has to dry and form a film before rain, dew, or heat interferes. In Florida, that means a painting schedule is built around humidity, dew point, and afternoon storms, not just the calendar.
excerpt: Humidity, dew point, surface heat, and afternoon storms decide when exterior paint can go on in Florida. How weather shapes the schedule.

body: Modern exterior paints, mostly 100% acrylic latex, dry in two stages. First, water evaporates from the film. Then the acrylic particles fuse together, a process called coalescence, to form a continuous, flexible film. Both stages depend on weather. Humidity slows evaporation, cold slows coalescence, and moisture on the surface interferes with both. Paint can feel dry to the touch long before it has formed a weather-resistant film.

When conditions are wrong, the results show up later: poor adhesion, sticky or soft paint, streaking, uneven sheen, and premature peeling. Understanding the main weather factors explains why a good painting crew sometimes waits even when the sky looks fine.

High relative humidity slows drying and keeps paint soft longer, which makes it more vulnerable to dirt, insects, and rain. The bigger risk is dew. The dew point is the temperature at which moisture in the air condenses onto surfaces. On many Florida nights and early mornings, surfaces cool to or below the dew point and become wet even without rain.

Paint manufacturers commonly recommend that the surface temperature be at least 5 degrees Fahrenheit above the dew point during application and early drying. If dew forms on fresh paint, a white or tan sticky residue of surfactants can rise to the surface, an effect called surfactant leaching, and the film may not cure properly.
bullets: Wait until morning dew has completely evaporated before painting.
Stop early enough in the afternoon for the film to set before evening dew forms.
Shaded and north-facing walls stay damp longer; schedule them later in the morning.

body: Florida walls in full sun can become much hotter than the air temperature. Painting a hot surface makes the paint dry too quickly, before it can level and bond, which leads to lap marks, brush marks, blistering, and weaker adhesion. Check the label for the maximum surface temperature as well as the minimum. An inexpensive infrared thermometer pointed at the wall tells you more than the air temperature on your phone, and it is worth checking each elevation before opening the can.

Experienced crews follow the shade around the house, painting the east side in the afternoon after the sun has moved off it and the west side in the morning. Dark colors absorb more heat, so they are especially sensitive to application in direct sun.

From late spring through summer, afternoon thunderstorms are routine across North Central Florida. Fresh latex paint needs time to set before rain; many products list a rain-ready time of a few hours under ideal conditions, but humidity and cooler temperatures stretch that out. Rain on fresh paint can wash out color, cause streaks and spots, or reduce adhesion.
Practical rules for the rainy season:
bullets: Start early and end early, giving the paint the most drying time before storms build.
Check radar throughout the day, not just the forecast the night before.
Do not paint surfaces that are still wet from the previous day's rain; check wood with a moisture meter.
Build weather days into any summer exterior schedule.

body: North Central Florida winters are mild, but cold fronts can bring nights near or below freezing. Most exterior latex paints have a minimum application temperature, often around 35 to 50 degrees Fahrenheit depending on the product, and that temperature must hold for the air and the surface during application and for several hours afterward. Painting late on a cool afternoon, when temperatures are falling, risks poor film formation and cracking.
On the plus side, winter and early spring often have low humidity and fewer storms, making them good painting seasons when you work in the warmer middle of the day.

For most homes in North Central Florida, October through May offers the most reliable exterior painting conditions: lower humidity, fewer storms, and more moderate surface temperatures. Spring pollen is a factor, so surfaces must be washed just before painting. Summer work is entirely possible with careful scheduling, but projects can take longer because of weather days.

Wind and pollen matter too. Spraying in steady wind wastes paint and spreads overspray onto cars, roofs, and plants, and a blustery spring day can blow dust and pollen into wet paint. Crews often brush and roll instead of spraying on windy days, or switch to sheltered elevations. Smoke from prescribed burns and agricultural fires, common in parts of North Central Florida, can leave grit on fresh paint, another reason to watch local conditions.

Interiors are a different story. With the air conditioning running, interior painting can be done any time of year, and it is a good use of the summer months. Our year-round exterior care calendar shows how to plan maintenance and painting across the seasons.

sections.h2: How a professional crew handles weather
body: A well-run exterior job is planned around conditions: washing and prep on marginal days, painting during the best part of the day, and checking surface temperature, dew point, and moisture before starting. Products such as moisture-tolerant primers and 100% acrylic topcoats are chosen with Florida weather in mind, and that is one reason our article on exterior paint lifespan in Florida stresses application conditions as much as the paint itself.

Precision Paint Experts schedules exterior painting across Alachua, Marion, Levy, Columbia, and Gilchrist counties, with summer work done earlier in the day while watching dew point and radar. faqs.q: Can you paint outside when it is humid?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. Paint dries more slowly in high humidity, so crews start after dew has evaporated, keep surfaces above the dew point, and finish early enough for the paint to set before evening dew or rain.

faqs.q: How long should exterior paint dry before rain?
faqs.a: It depends on the product and conditions. Many exterior latex paints need a few hours in good conditions, but humidity and cooler temperatures extend that time. Check the label and the radar.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to paint a house in Florida?
faqs.a: In North Central Florida, October through May usually offers the best conditions, with lower humidity and fewer afternoon storms than summer.

faqs.q: What happens if dew forms on fresh paint?
faqs.a: Dew can cause surfactant leaching, a sticky white or tan residue, and can interfere with curing. Residue can often be washed off once the paint cures, but painting too late in the day is best avoided.
